trust_decision.summary: Whether the driver may put the authentication answer for the server-named initial plugin (the clear-text password for mysql_clear_password) on the wire in the initial HandshakeResponse. That needs a secure transport whose server identity is already verified, not just deferred to a later fingerprint check. At the pinned commit the only gate is an SSL-capability check inside the encoder; the fix moves the decision to StandardClient.handleAuthentication before the response is built.

landing_point.why: This is the only place that writes the clear-text password into the initial-handshake response, and it already holds a 'Cannot send password in clear if SSL is not enabled' guard. Grepping for mysql_clear_password or 'clear' leads straight here.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/main/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/message/client/HandshakeResponse.java:141-144 (the existing SSL-capability guard in the encoder, in another package; the fix removes it and replaces it in StandardClient, fix.diff:439-447)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: HandshakeResponse already refuses clear text without SSL, and the self-signed case is 'already handled' by the fingerprint check at the OK packet (StandardClient.java:526-549) and by the auth-switch gate (StandardClient.java:490-502). A solver can argue the initial path is covered and not see that the password has already left before either of those checks runs.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Self-signed TLS without a CA ('MitM-proof without CA') must keep working for MitM-proof plugins (native, ed25519, parsec) with a non-empty password, validated by fingerprint at the OK packet. mysql_clear_password must keep working over CA-verified TLS, over sslMode=trust and over a local unix socket. An over-broad fix (refuse every self-signed cert, or refuse clear password whenever SSL is used) breaks these.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: full-auth (0x04) branch sends the clear password gated on configured sslMode; a copy that drops the sslFingerPrintValidation term, or gates on SSL capability only, would leak under deferred identity
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This branch already makes its own local clear-text decision from sslMode instead of verified identity, so a maintainer could easily write the weaker variant.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a re-authentication path (redirect or a planted COM_CHANGE_USER / pool re-auth packet) that builds its own auth response with the initial-plugin shortcut instead of going through handleAuthentication
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The redirect code already re-runs connection setup with a rebuilt Configuration; a change-user packet in message.client next to HandshakeResponse is a natural feature that would copy the encoder's clear-text branch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: plugin-level guard that checks sslMode != DISABLE/TRUST and the fingerprint flag but not unix-socket/plain-TCP; a second clear-text plugin (e.g. a token/IAM plugin) with only this guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Plugins are loaded through ServiceLoader and each one carries its own guard, so adding a token plugin with a copied guard is plausible.

O9_family: CWE-522 insufficiently protected credentials: clear-text secret sent before the TLS peer identity is verified (check-before-send ordering)

O10_build.project_tests: The fix adds src/test/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/unit/client/RogueServerCredentialLeakTest.java, which uses an in-process loopback rogue server plus a test keystore src/test/resources/loopback-server.p12 (fix.diff:79-353), so no DB is needed. Existing related tests are src/test/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/unit/client/MariaDbX509DeferredIdentityTrustManagerTest.java (unit) and integration/SslTest.java and integration/ConnectionTest.java, which need a live MariaDB.
